name: markdown-renderer
title: markdown-renderer
description: The Universal Markdown renderer: draws a markdown string (headings, lists, tables, code, links, images) or a typed-block document (prose, key facts, steps, lists, tables, fine print — tabbed when its groups call for it), under an optional titled header with a streaming indicator.

definition.name: markdown-renderer
definition.description: The Universal Markdown renderer: draws a markdown string (headings, lists, tables, code, links, images) or a typed-block document (prose, key facts, steps, lists, tables, fine print — tabbed when its groups call for it), under an optional titled header with a streaming indicator.
definition.whenToUse: Render Universal Markdown, in either of its two forms. Given a markdown string it draws formatted prose; given typed blocks (sections) it draws the structured document, tabs and all. Any surface showing a record's body copy, a generated report or an agent's document uses this. Pick the streaming chat component instead only for a conversational reply streaming token by token.

title.description: The header above the document. Empty means no header.

markdown.description: The document as one markdown string: headings, lists, tables, code, links, images. Use this OR sections, never both.

streamingLabel.description: The words shown beside the indicator while the document is still arriving.

placeholderText.description: What stands in the empty frame before any content has arrived.

body.description: The passage, in Markdown, taken from the source. Headings, lists, emphasis and links are all allowed. Never rewrite the source's meaning, and never add facts it does not state.

items.description: The question and answer pairs the source states AS SUCH. Never reframe ordinary copy as questions, and skip any pair whose answer merely restates its question.

title.description: The question, as a reader would ask it.

body.description: The answer the source gives. Answer it; never restate the question.

facts.description: The figures, in the order the source states them. Every value is quoted from the source, never calculated, converted or rounded, and never invented to fill the row out.

label.description: What the figure counts, in the source's own words. Two or three words.

value.description: The figure exactly as the source states it, with its unit or symbol: '18%', 'SAR 750', '29 million'. Never a phrase, never a clause. Move a modifier like 'more than' or 'up to' into the qualifier rather than shortening the figure to fit: a truncated number is WRONG, where a longer qualifier is merely longer.

qualifier.description: The condition or period the figure carries, short. Empty when the source attaches none. It must be a COMPLETE phrase: if it will not fit, drop words until it does ('ATMs worldwide'), never stop mid-phrase ('ATMs and financial institutions within the King').

columns.description: The column headers, in the source's own words. Two to five; a table wider than that belongs as several sections.

rows.description: The rows, each a list of cells in the SAME ORDER as the columns and the same length. Every cell is quoted from the source, never calculated or filled in to complete the grid.

value.description: One row's cells, in the same order as the columns and the same length.

title.description: The warning itself, in one line. State the consequence, not the topic.

value.description: Propose this passage only from what the source actually says, in the person's own words where they exist. Never write on their behalf to fill the box: this is a field they are expected to write themselves.

label.description: The question, written as the statement the person is agreeing to or declining: 'Send me alerts about new deals'. Never phrase it so that OFF is the agreeable answer, and never ask for a consent the source does not require.
label.preview: Send me alerts about new deals

help.description: One line of help the source gives about the code, such as how long it lasts or what to do if it does not arrive. Empty when the source says nothing.

options.description: The options the source defines, in its own order and its own words. Never invent an option, never drop one because it seems unlikely, and never add 'Other' unless the source offers it.

description.description: One line the source gives about what agreeing means in practice, such as how often, or what it is used for. Empty when the question says it all.
description.preview: Occasional email, and never more than once a week.

sections.description: The document as typed blocks in reading order: prose, key facts, steps, lists, tables, fine print.

default.heading: What it is
default.body: A passage of body copy, with **inline marks** and links.

tabbed.description: Whether the document draws as tabs or as one page. Decided by the shaping pass from the blocks' own groups, never set by hand.
